app.name: Bugaboo

error.auth.wrong-second-step-code: That code is not right. Check the code in your app, or use one of your backup codes.
error.auth.wrong-setup-code: That setup code is not right. Copy it again from the window where Bugaboo is running.
error.auth.password-too-short: Choose a password with at least 12 characters. Length matters more than special characters.
error.auth.password-breached: That password is on lists of passwords that are tried first. Please choose another one.
error.auth.invitation-invalid: This invitation does not work. It may have run out or been used already. Ask for a new one.
error.auth.sign-up-refused: You cannot sign up here. Ask an administrator to invite you.
error.auth.passkey-rejected: The passkey could not be checked. Please try again.
error.request.wrong-token: Your sign-in does not fit this page any more. Sign in again and then try again.
error.auth.second-step-required: Before you go on, set up your second step. Your administrator asks for it, and it keeps your account safe even if your password leaks.
error.auth.access-key-not-allowed: An access key cannot do that. Sign in with your password to change your own sign-in details.
error.access.forbidden: You are not allowed to do that.
error.request.invalid: Something in your request is not valid. Check what you typed and try again.
error.request.unknown-field: We could not find one of the fields you asked for. Check the field names and try again.
error.request.bad-cursor: This list changed. Start again from the top.
error.request.wrong-origin: That did not come from a Bugaboo page. Reload the page and try again.
error.request.method-not-allowed: Bugaboo does not do that here.
error.request.timed-out: Your request took too long to arrive. Please try again.
error.request.too-large: That is too big to send.
error.edit.version-changed: Not saved yet: someone changed this after you started. Your text is still here.
error.edit.lock-lost: Not saved yet: your editing time ran out. Your text is kept as a draft.
error.edit.in-progress: Someone is editing this right now. Try again when they have finished.
error.edit.taken-over: Not saved yet: someone took over the editing. Your text is kept as a draft.
error.search.invalid: The search has a mistake. Read the notes next to it and correct it.
error.search.too-slow: This search took too long. Add a filter to narrow it down and try again.
error.rate-limit.exceeded: Too many tries. Please wait a little and try again.
error.server.unavailable: Bugaboo is not available right now. Please try again in a moment.
error.server.internal: Something went wrong on our side. Nothing you did caused this.
setting.security.session-idle-minutes.he: How many minutes without activity pass before people are signed out automatically. Between 5 minutes and 24 hours.
setting.security.two-step-required.help: Ask everyone to use two-step sign-in. People who have not set it up are asked to do so the next time they sign in.
How many hours a sign-in can last at most, even when someone keeps working. After that, people sign in again. Between 1 hour and 30 days (720 hours).
setting.auth.access-key-default-days.hel: How many days a new access key lives when the person picks no other date. Between 1 and 365 days.
setting.auth.access-key-longest-days.hel: The most days an access key can live, whatever date the person picks. Between 1 and 365 days.
setting.auth.sign-up-enabled.help: Let people ask for an account on their own, without an invitation. Bugaboo sends an e-mail to the e-mail address they give, and the account is created only when they open the link in it, so this works only while e-mail is on.
setting.content.image-hosts.name: Hosts that images may come from
setting.content.image-hosts.help: The hosts that may show images in descriptions and comments, as a list separated by commas, like images.example.com. Write only the host name, without https:// and without a path. Leave the list empty to show no image from other hosts.
setting.auth.sign-up-domains.help: The e-mail domains that may sign up on their own, as a list separated by commas, like example.com. Leave the list empty to let every address sign up while signing up is on, so write your domains in first.
setting.ui.locked-why: An administrator chose this for everyone, so you cannot change it here.
setting.ui.lock-help: While this is locked, nobody can choose their own value.
setting.ui.source-hidden-project: From a project you cannot see
setting.ui.example-moment: Right now, a time looks like this: {moment}
setting.page.region-intro: These choices are kept with you, so they follow you to every browser you sign in from.
setting.page.start-page-intro: Choose the page Bugaboo opens after you sign in.
setting.page.sign-in-rules-intro: How long people stay signed in, and the rules for signing in. They apply to everybody.
setting.page.security-intro: What the text that people write may show.
setting.page.themes-intro: The organization's choice of look. People can choose their own, unless you lock a setting.
setting.appearance.mode.help: The colors Bugaboo uses on your screen. Match my device follows the light or dark setting of your device.
setting.appearance.light-theme.help: The theme Bugaboo shows when your device is light. It counts when you choose Match my device.
setting.appearance.dark-theme.help: The theme Bugaboo shows when your device is dark. It counts when you choose Match my device.
setting.appearance.spacing.help: How close together things are. Compact fits more on a page.
setting.appearance.larger-text.help: Enlarges all text by a step.
setting.appearance.less-motion.help: Fewer moving effects. Bugaboo also follows the setting of your device.
setting.appearance.issue-view.name: Open issues in
setting.appearance.issue-view.help: Where an issue opens: in the focus view, which gives it most of the page, or in a side panel next to the list.
setting.region.time-zone.name: Time zone
setting.region.time-zone.help: The time zone for the times you see. Match my device uses the time zone of your device.
setting.region.date-format.name: Date format
setting.region.number-format.name: Number format
setting.region.number-format.help: How big numbers and decimals are written.
setting.region.first-day.name: First day of the week
setting.region.first-day.help: The day a week starts on in calendars.
setting.start.page.name: Start page
setting.start.page.help: The page Bugaboo opens after you sign in.
setting.shortcuts.keys.name: Your own keys
setting.shortcuts.keys.help: The keys you chose for keyboard shortcuts. A shortcut you did not change keeps its usual keys.
setting.window.sizes.name: Your window sizes
setting.window.sizes.help: The size you gave each form that opens as a window. A form you did not resize keeps its usual size.
setting.security.two-step-required.name: Two-step sign-in for everybody
setting.auth.sign-up-enabled.name: Sign up without an invitation
setting.auth.sign-up-domains.name: E-mail domains that may sign up
setting.auth.access-key-default-days.nam: Access key lasts (days), when no date is picked
setting.auth.access-key-longest-days.nam: Longest an access key can last (days)
cookie.session.purpose: Keeps you signed in on this device. Bugaboo removes it when you sign out or when your sign-in runs out.
cookie.csrf.purpose: Protects you from other websites that try to get Bugaboo to do something in your name.

server.setup-code: Setup is open. Open Bugaboo in your browser and enter this setup code to create the first administrator: {code}
server.setup-code-hint: The code works once and changes every time Bugaboo starts.
server.self-signed: HTTPS uses a certificate created by Bugaboo, so browsers warn until you trust it. The certificate is in {path}.
server.signal-failed: Bugaboo could not listen for the stop signal (Ctrl+C), so it cannot be stopped cleanly.
server.port-busy: Port {port} is busy or not allowed. Choose another port.
config.file-unreadable: The settings file {path} could not be read: {reason}
config.file-invalid: The settings file {path} is not valid: {reason}
config.file-unknown-key: The settings file {path} has a setting Bugaboo does not know: {name}. Known settings are: {known}.
config.file-wrong-type: The setting {name} in {path} must be a text, a number or a list of texts.
config.port-missing: No port is set. Set port in bugaboo.toml, set BUGABOO_PORT, or start with --port.
config.port-invalid: The port {value} is not a number from 1 to 65535.
config.address-invalid: The address {value} is not an IP address such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1.
config.data-dir-empty: The data folder is empty text. Give the path of a folder.
config.database-invalid: The database address must start with sqlite: or postgres:// (or postgresql://).
config.tls-mode-invalid: The HTTPS mode {value} is not known. Use self-signed, files or off.
config.tls-files-missing: HTTPS mode files needs both tls_cert and tls_key.
config.tls-files-unused: tls_cert and tls_key are only used with HTTPS mode files. Remove them or change the mode.
config.tls-off-public: HTTPS cannot be switched off on {address}, because anyone on the network could read what is sent. Use 127.0.0.1 or ::1, or list the proxy that adds HTTPS in trusted_proxies.
config.public-url-invalid: The public address {value} is not a web address like https://bugaboo.example.com.
config.public-url-needed: Bugaboo listens on {address}, so it cannot know the address people type in the browser. Set public_url, for example https://bugaboo.example.com.
config.public-url-proxy: A proxy is listed in trusted_proxies, so people reach Bugaboo through the address of the proxy, which Bugaboo cannot know. Set public_url, for example https://bugaboo.example.com.
config.proxy-invalid: The trusted proxy {value} is not an IP address.
config.log-level-invalid: The log level {value} is not known. Use error, warn, info or debug.

setup.welcome: Welcome to Bugaboo. A few questions, then your answers are saved in a settings file. Press Enter to accept the answer in brackets.
setup.ask.data-dir: Where should Bugaboo keep its data? Give the path of a folder.
setup.ask.address: Who should be able to open Bugaboo? Type 127.0.0.1 for this computer only, or 0.0.0.0 for everyone who can reach this computer.
setup.ask.port: Which port should Bugaboo listen on?
setup.ask.tls: How should the connection be secured (HTTPS)? Type self-signed to let Bugaboo create its own certificate, files to use a certificate you already have, or off for plain HTTP (only on this computer or behind a proxy).
setup.ask.tls-key: Where is the private key file?
setup.ask.public-url: Which web address will people type to reach Bugaboo? For example https://bugaboo.example.com
setup.ask.database: Which database? Type built-in for the database inside the data folder, or a sqlite: or postgres:// address.
setup.ask.replace: The settings file {path} already exists. Replace it? Type yes or no.
setup.exists: The settings file {path} already exists. Add --overwrite to replace it.
setup.input-ended: The questions were not all answered, so nothing was saved.
setup.next: Start Bugaboo with: bugaboo serve. The first start shows a setup code in that window. You need it to create the first administrator in your browser.
setup.service-hint: To have Bugaboo start with the computer, run: bugaboo service install
security-log.valid: The security log is intact: {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} checked.
security-log.head: The last entry is number {seq}. Its hash starts with {hash}. Keep a copy of this to compare later.
security-log.unanchored: Nothing vouches for the end of the log, because its anchor file is missing or empty. Someone could cut entries off the end without anybody noticing.
security-log.broken: The security log is broken at entry {seq}: {reason}
security-log.unreadable: The security log could not be read.
security-log.reason.gap: an entry is missing, appears twice or is out of order.
security-log.reason.broken-link: an entry does not match the entry before it.
security-log.reason.changed-content: an entry was changed after it was written.
security-log.reason.checkpoint: entries were deleted without a signed checkpoint, or the checkpoint is wrong.
security-log.reason.truncated: entries at the end of the log were cut off or rewritten.
security-log.reason.anchor: the anchor file that vouches for the end of the log was changed.
security-log.reason.behind: the database lacks the newest entries that the anchor file knows of. Check whether the database was restored from an older backup or lost its last writes. If neither happened, someone removed entries.
keys.rotated: Created a new master key and used it for {secrets, plural, one {# stored secret} other {# stored secrets}}. Back up the key files again.
keys.exported: Copied the key files into {path}. They can read everything Bugaboo stores in secret: keep them in a safe place, away from the database backup.
keys.export-exists: The folder {path} already holds a copy of a key file. Choose another folder, so no copy is overwritten.
keys.export-failed: The key files could not be copied: {reason}
service.needs-admin: Installing or removing a service needs administrator rights. On Windows, open the terminal as an administrator. On Linux, run the command with sudo.
service.unit-folder-unknown: systemd did not say where the units belong that an administrator installs, and Bugaboo does not guess it. Ask your system: systemd-path systemd-system-conf
service.answer-not-trusted: The system named {path}, but root does not own it alone or other accounts can change it, so Bugaboo does not use it.
service.program-not-found: The program {program} was not found on the search path (PATH). Install it, or add its folder to the search path, and run the command again.
service.unsupported: Bugaboo can run as a service on Windows and on Linux with systemd. This computer has neither.
service.no-settings: There is no settings file at {path}. Run bugaboo setup first, or name the file with --config.
service.installed: The service {name} is installed and started. It runs as the account {account} and starts with the computer.
service.setup-code: Nobody has created an administrator yet. The setup code for the first administrator is saved in {path}. Read it there, and enter it in your browser.
service.exists: The service {name} is installed already. Remove it first with: bugaboo service uninstall
service.removed: The service {name} is removed. Your data stays where it is.
service.not-a-service: This command is for the service manager. To start Bugaboo yourself, use: bugaboo serve
server.setup-code-file: Setup is open. The setup code is saved in {path}. Read it there and enter it in your browser to create the first administrator.
service.stop-timeout: The service {name} did not stop in time. Stop it in the Services window and try again.
validation.email: Type an e-mail address like name@example.com.
field.password-help: At least 12 characters. A few words in a row give a good password.
field.name: Your name
field.confirm-password-help: Type your password again to confirm it is you.
home.title: Welcome, {name}
home.admin: You can look after this server. Organization settings shows what you may do there.
page.not-found.title: This page does not exist
page.not-found.text: The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved.
sign-in.title: Sign in to Bugaboo
second-step.title: One more step
second-step.intro: Your password is right. Your account asks for a second check before it opens.
second-step.code-help: Type the six-digit code from your code app. If you cannot use the app, type one of your backup codes.
second-step.passkey-help: Use the fingerprint, face or screen lock of this device.
sign-up.title: Create an account
sign-up.closed: Creating your own account is switched off here. Ask an administrator to invite you.
invitation.title: Join Bugaboo
invitation.intro: You are invited. Your account will use the e-mail address {email}.
invitation.incomplete: This link is not complete. Open the whole link that you were sent.
first-run.title: Welcome to Bugaboo
first-run.code.intro: Bugaboo was just installed, so nobody has an account yet. So that only you can create the first one, Bugaboo shows a setup code where it is running.
first-run.code.where: Look in the window where Bugaboo is running for the line that starts with Setup is open. If Bugaboo runs as a service, the code is in the file setup-code.txt inside its data folder.
first-run.code.label: Setup code
first-run.code.help: It looks like k7q2-x9mf-3hd8-vt4w. Capital letters and hyphens do not matter.
first-run.account.title: Create the first administrator
first-run.account.intro: An administrator can invite people and look after the server. This account is the first one.
first-run.safer.title: Keep your account safe
first-run.safer.intro: A password alone can be guessed or stolen. You can add a second check now, or later in Sign-in & security.
first-run.done.title: You are all set
first-run.done.text: Your account is ready and you are signed in.
security.title: Sign-in & security
security.intro: How you prove that it is you, and how to keep your account safe.
security.password.title: Password
security.password.changed: Your password is changed. You are signed out everywhere else.
passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: A passkey lets you sign in with the fingerprint, face or screen lock of your device instead of typing a password. It can also be your second step.
passkeys.unavailable: Passkeys need Bugaboo to be opened with a web address that has a name, not a number. Ask the person who runs Bugaboo to set the public address.
passkeys.name: Name for this passkey
passkeys.remove-text: You can no longer sign in with this passkey. Type your password to confirm.
passkeys.cancelled: The passkey was not used. You can try again.
code-app.title: Code app
code-app.intro: A code app on your phone shows a new six-digit code every 30 seconds. You type it after your password.
code-app.on: The code app is set up.
code-app.off: The code app is not set up.
code-app.scan: Scan this picture with your code app.
code-app.qr-alt: QR picture for your code app
code-app.key-label: Cannot scan? Type this key into your app
code-app.confirm-help: Type the six-digit code that the app shows now.
code-app.switched-on: The code app is switched on. Save your backup codes now.
code-app.turn-off-text: Your account will be less safe. Type your password to confirm.
code-app.turned-off: The code app is switched off.
backup.title: Backup codes
backup.intro: Each backup code works once. They are for when you cannot use your code app. Keep them somewhere safe.
backup.left: {count, plural, one {# backup code is left} other {# backup codes are left}}.
backup.shown-once: These codes are shown only now. Save them before you leave this page.
sessions.title: Where you're signed in
sessions.intro: Each line is a place where you are signed in, like a browser. Sign out of the ones you do not know.
sessions.list: Places where you are signed in
sessions.unknown-device: A browser we do not know
sessions.everywhere-text: You will be signed out of every browser, this one included, and have to sign in again. Your access keys are deleted and stop working too.
sessions.cut-off: Only the newest places are shown.
invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.intro: An invitation is a link that lets one person create their account. It works once and runs out after 7 days.
invitations.link-help: Bugaboo cannot send e-mail yet. Copy this link and send it to the person. It is shown only now.
sign-up-policy.title: Signing up without an invitation
sign-up-policy.intro: When this is on, anyone who can open Bugaboo can ask for an account without being invited. It works only while e-mail is on, because the e-mail that lets them create the account goes to their address.
sign-up-policy.switch: Let people create their own account
sign-up-policy.domains: E-mail domains that may sign up
sign-up-policy.domains-help: One domain per line, like example.com. Only addresses of these domains can sign up.
sign-up-policy.warning: No domain is listed, so everyone who can reach Bugaboo can ask for an account. The e-mail goes to the address they give, so only a person who can read that address can create one.
sign-up-policy.confirm-text: No domain is listed. Everybody who can reach Bugaboo will be able to create an account.
server-status.title: Server status
server-status.intro: How this Bugaboo server is doing.
server-status.uptime: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}, {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
server-status.database.built-in: The built-in database in the data folder
server-status.certificate.valid: Valid until {date}, which is {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} from now.
server-status.certificate.soon: Valid until {date}, which is only {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} from now. Renew it soon.
server-status.certificate.expired: This certificate ran out on {date}. Browsers refuse it.
server-status.certificate.none: Not shown. Either another program in front of Bugaboo handles HTTPS, or the certificate file cannot be read.
server.setup-code-file-failed: Setup is open, but the setup code could not be saved in {path}: {reason}. Stop Bugaboo and start it in a terminal with: bugaboo serve. The terminal shows the code.
keys.not-owner: The data folder {path} belongs to the account {owner}, and you are using another one. A command run from here could leave files that the Bugaboo service cannot read. Run it as {owner}: {how}
keys.no-access: This account cannot read and change the key files in {path}. If Bugaboo runs as a service, run the command as the account that runs it: {how}
keys.how-windows: On Windows that account is {owner}. It has no password, so you cannot sign in as it: stop the service, start a terminal as that account with a tool that can do this, and run: {command}
keys.export-not-private: The folder {path} can be opened by other accounts on this computer. Choose a folder that only you can open, or a new one, so the key files are not left where others can copy them.
data-folder.not-a-data-folder: The folder {path} has other files in it and does not look like a Bugaboo data folder. Installing the service would change who owns them. Choose an empty folder or a Bugaboo data folder as the data folder in your settings.
service.settings-is-link: The settings file {path} is a link. Installing would change the rights of the file it points to. Name the real file with --config.
service.settings-in-data: The settings file {path} is inside the data folder, which the account that runs the service can write to. Move the file out of the data folder, so that the service cannot change its own settings.
service.settings-folder-open: The folder {path} that holds the settings file can be changed by other accounts. Keep the settings file in a folder that only administrators can change, for example /etc/bugaboo.
service.settings-folder-owner: The folder {path} that holds the settings file does not belong to the administrator account (root). Keep the settings file in a folder that root owns, for example /etc/bugaboo.
service.data-folder-real: The data folder {path} is a link. The service uses the folder it leads to: {real}.
window.resize-keys: To change the size of this window, press Ctrl and Alt with the arrow keys.
search-index.opened-address: Opened the database that the settings name by an address (the address is not shown; it can hold a password).
search-index.data-older: The data in this installation is older than this program. Start the server once: it brings the data up to date and builds the index again by itself. Then run this command again if you still need it.
search-index.data-newer: The data in this installation was changed by a newer version of this program. Use the newer version for this command.
search-index.rebuilt: The index of the text search was built again for {issues, plural, one {# issue} other {# issues}}.

search.bar.text-filter-text: Simple search has no picker for this filter. Change it as text.

search.bar.pick-search: Type the start of a name
search.bar.issue-search: Issue ID or words of the title

search.share-none: There is nothing you may share with.
search.share-note: Everyone sees only the issues and fields they are allowed to see.
search.project-list-stop: Stop using as the list of {project}
search.help-fields-text: Write the name of a field, then what it should be.
search.help-comparing-text: Compare with is, is not, in a list, or with bigger and smaller.
search.help-time-text: Days are written like 2026-12-31. Words like today and this week also work.
search.help-relations-text: Look inside a project, or at the issues around one issue.
search.help-text-text: Find words in titles and texts. Put more than one word in quotes.

search.help-your-fields-text: The fields you may search by, each with the word that stands for it in the search.
search.bar.duration-help: Write a length of time, for example {hours}, {minutes} or {both}.
search.bar.not-a-duration: Write a length of time like {hours} or {both}.
search.mistake.expected-filter: A filter is missing here. Start it with the name of a field, like “priority”.
search.mistake.expected-operator: What should be true of “{field}”? Write for example “{is}”, “{contains}” or “{in}”.
search.mistake.expected-in: After “{in}” write “{last}” and a number, or a list of values in brackets.
search.mistake.expected-list-next: Write a comma and the next value, or close the list with a bracket.
search.mistake.expected-duration: Write a whole number before “{hours}” or “{minutes}”, like 2 {hours}, 45 {minutes} or 1 {hour} 30 {minutes}.
search.mistake.expected-count: Write a whole number of 1 or more here.
search.mistake.expected-unit: Write a unit of time here: {units}.
search.mistake.expected-text: Write the text to look for here, in quotes.
search.mistake.expected-short-name: Write the short name of a project here, in capital letters, like WEB.
search.mistake.expected-issue-id: Write an Issue ID here, like WEB-142.
search.mistake.expected-continue: After a filter you can write “{and}”, “{or}” or “{sort} {by}”.
search.mistake.expected-continue-closing: After a filter you can write “{and}” or “{or}”, or close the bracket.
search.mistake.expected-sort-field: Write the field to sort by here.
search.mistake.word-too-long: A word in this text is too long to be found. Split it into shorter words.
search.mistake.prefix-too-short: A word that ends in * needs at least {limit} letters before the *.
search.mistake.reserved-word: “{word}” is a word of the search language. To search for it, put it in quotes.
search.mistake.unclosed-quote: This text in quotes does not end. Add the closing quote.
search.mistake.not-a-date: “{text}” is not a day in the calendar. Write a day like 2026-10-25.
search.mistake.too-deep: There are too many brackets inside brackets.
search.mistake.unknown-field-did-you-mea: There is no field called “{field}”. Did you mean “{suggestion}”?
search.mistake.unknown-choice-did-you-me: “{field}” has no choice called “{value}”. Did you mean “{suggestion}”?
search.mistake.wrong-duration: “{field}” needs a length of time here, like 2 {hours}, 45 {minutes} or 1 {hour} 30 {minutes}.
search.mistake.wrong-date: “{field}” needs a day like 2026-10-25, or a word like today.
search.mistake.wrong-text: “{field}” needs a text here. Put it in quotes.
search.mistake.wrong-person: “{field}” needs the name of a person here, or “{me}”.
search.mistake.wrong-issue: “{field}” needs an Issue ID here, like WEB-142.
search.mistake.too-many-filters: A search can have at most {limit} filters; each value in a list counts as one.
search.mistake.too-many-sort-keys: A search can be sorted by at most {limit} fields.
search.mistake.too-long: This search is too long. Please shorten it.
search.mistake.too-many-steps: A search can look at most {limit} steps away.
search.mistake.too-many-words: A text to find can have at most {limit} different words.

access-keys.never: No key can invite people, change who has which role, change the settings of the organization, or change how you sign in. You do that here, where you are signed in.
access-keys.help.permissions: The key can do only what you tick below, and only what you can do yourself.
access-keys.projects-help: Tick none for every project. A key for some projects works in them and in the projects inside them, and gives nothing for the whole organization.

setting.files.max-megabytes.help: The most megabytes one file added to an issue or a comment may have. A project can allow less than the organization, never more. Between 1 and 100.
setting.files.blocked-types.name: Types of file that are never accepted
setting.files.blocked-types.help: File types the organization never accepts, as a list separated by commas, like exe, bat. A file is refused when its content or its name has one of these types.
setting.issues.id-mode.name: Issue IDs
setting.issues.id-mode.help: Random IDs (like WEB-K7Q2X) hide how many issues there are and how fast they come. Counting IDs (like WEB-142) are easy to say aloud. When you change this, every issue of the project gets a new ID; the old IDs keep working.
setting.issues.id-length.name: Length of random issue IDs
setting.issues.id-length.help: How many letters and digits a random issue ID has after the dash. Between 4 and 8. It grows by itself when the short ones run out.
issue-types.intro: An issue type says what kind of issue it is: a bug, a task, a feature or a goal. Everybody who creates an issue picks one of these. Retire a type to stop new issues of it; the issues that have it keep it.
issue-types.nothing: No issue type has that name.
issue-types.create-intro: A new type goes to the end of the list. Pick an icon so people find it quickly.
issue-types.retire-help: A retired type is not offered for new issues. The issues that have it keep it and can still be changed. You can offer it again later.
error.field.too-short: That is shorter than this field allows.
error.field.too-long: That is longer than this field allows.
error.field.too-small: That is lower than this field allows.
error.field.too-big: That is higher than this field allows.
error.field.no-match: That does not have the form this field asks for.
error.field.wrong-value: That is not a value this field can hold.
error.field.unknown-choice: That choice is not offered by this field.
error.field.unknown-reference: That person, group or issue cannot be chosen here.
error.field.not-here: This field is not used here.
field-permissions.type-help: These levels count for issues of every type, unless a level is set for one type below.
field-permissions.type-help-chosen: A level set here counts for issues of this type only, and wins over the level for all types. Where nothing is set for this type, the level for all types counts.
fields.intro: Fields are the pieces of information on an issue or a project. Add the fields your organization needs, and decide who sees and fills in each one under Field permissions.
fields.nothing: There are no fields of your own yet. Create one below.
fields.create-intro: Start with what kind of information the field holds. You can change everything else later, except the kind.
fields.field-choices-help: One choice on each line. You can change names, colors and icons on the field page.
fields.never-to-assistant: Never send this field to the assistant
fields.default-help: The value a new issue or project starts with. Leave it empty for none.
fields.choices-help: Use the arrows to change the order. Retire a choice to stop offering it for new values; the values already set stay. Combine a choice with another one to move every value over.
fields.rule-pattern-help: The whole text has to match. For example, [A-Z]+-[0-9]+ matches CAB-12.
fields.rules-not-a-number: One of the rules is not in the form this field uses: a number, a length of time or a day like 2026-10-25.
fields.look-preview: The look in all four themes
fields.used-everywhere: {count, plural, =0 {No project has a value yet.} one {1 project has a value.} other {# projects have a value.}}
fields.used-in-projects: {count, plural, =0 {No project you can see uses it.} one {Used in 1 project.} other {Used in # projects.}}
fields.scope-projects-list: Projects the field is limited to
fields.scope-types-help: Tick the issue types that have the field. With none ticked, every issue type has it.
fields.see-help: Each role sees a field as Hidden, Can see or Can change. A new field starts with Can see for everyone who sees the project, and Can change from Team member up.
fields.retire-help: A retired field is no longer offered for new values. The values already set stay on the issues and projects.
fields.not-a-decimal: Type a number, with a point for the decimal part.
fields.not-a-duration: Type a length of time like 1h 30m.
fields.combine-text: Every value of {name} becomes {into}, in every issue and project that has it, and {name} is retired. Each of those issues gets a record in its history. This cannot be taken back.
fields.used-more: {count, plural, one {And # more project.} other {And # more projects.}}
issues.title: Issues
conflict.sentence: Not saved: {who} changed {changes}{timed, select, true { {ago}} other {}}.
conflict.sentence-plain: Not saved: {who} changed this issue{timed, select, true { {ago}} other {}}.
issues.no-issue-type: This project offers no issue type. Ask who looks after the project.
issues.missing-title: Write a title first, then you can create and start another.
issues.missing-type: Choose an issue type first, then you can create and start another.
issues.missing-project: Choose a project first, then you can create and start another.
issues.ready-to-create: Nothing is missing: you can create the issue.
issues.draft-kept: Your draft is kept if you close this form.
issues.draft-found-form: You have a draft of a new issue from {when}.
issues.nothing: There are no issues here yet.
issues.read-only: Only people whose role allows it can change {field}.
issues.ask-for-intro: Before this issue can go to {to}, fill in:
issues.ask-for-description: Write the description of the issue first: this change needs it.
issues.assign-search: Search the people of the project
issues.assign-nothing: Nobody in this project has that name.
issues.assign-only-you: Nobody else is offered here: people you cannot see by name are not listed.
editing.elsewhere: You are editing {thing} in another window. Save or close it there. If that window is gone, wait a minute and try again.
editing.draft-found: You have a draft of {thing} from {when}.
editing.lost-ran-out: Not saved yet: you were away for a while, so your editing time ran out. Your text is kept.
editing.lost-taken-over: Not saved yet: {name} took over the editing. Your text is kept.
editing.lost-changed: Not saved yet: {name} changed {thing} after you. Your text is kept.
editing.text-kept: What you typed is kept as a draft:
editing.text-kept-on-close: What you typed is kept as a draft if you close this. Open it again to continue.
issues.changed-after-you: The description changed after you started.
issues.changed-after-you-by: {name} changed the description after you started.
issues.compare-intro: Your text is next to the newer version. For each paragraph that differs, choose which one to keep.
issues.compare-keep: Which text to keep for paragraph {number}
shortcut.change-status: Change the status of the open issue
shortcut.assign: Choose who the open issue is assigned to
shortcut.edit-description: Edit the description of the open issue
issues.selected: {count, plural, one {# issue is ticked} other {# issues are ticked}}
issues.changed-own: {count, plural, one {# field changed.} other {# fields changed.}}
fields.pick-no-groups: There are no groups you can choose.
many-changes-skip.not-found: It was deleted, or you can no longer see it
many-changes-skip.not-allowed: You may not change it this way
many-changes-skip.type-missing: The other project did not offer its issue type
many-changes-skip.label-not-here: The project of the issue does not offer the label group of that label
many-changes-skip.field-missing: It has a value in a field the other project does not use
many-changes-skip.tag-not-here: It has a tag that is not for the other project
many-changes-skip.same-issue: An issue cannot be related to itself
many-changes-skip.limit-reached: It already has as many of these as it can hold
many-changes-skip.field-rule: A value of the issue breaks the rule of its field
many-changes-skip.not-valid: This change cannot be applied to it
many-changes-skip.workflow: Its workflow does not allow this status change
error.tag.not-here: That tag is only for other projects. Choose another tag or ask who looks after tags.
error.label.not-offered: This project does not offer the label group of that label. Choose another label, or ask who looks after labels.
error.label.pick-one-conflict: Some issues have more than one label of this label group already, so it cannot be a label group to pick one from. Take the extra labels off first.
projects.preview-summary: {changed, plural, =0 {Nobody} one {# person} other {# people}} will gain or lose access or change role in the projects you can see.
labels.intro: Labels sort issues by label groups you choose, such as Area or Customer. Tags are free words that anybody who can change an issue can add to it.
labels.groups-nothing: No label group has that name.
labels.groups-none-yet: There are no label groups yet. Create the first one below.
labels.labels-none-yet: There are no labels yet. Create the first one below.
labels.tags-none-yet: There are no tags yet. A tag starts when you put it on an issue.
labels.create-label-group-intro: A label group keeps labels that belong together. Tick the box when an issue may have only one label of the label group.
labels.field-pick-one: An issue gets at most one label of this label group
labels.create-label-intro: A label has a name, a color and, if you like, a label group.
labels.retire-help: A retired one can no longer be put on issues. The issues that have it keep it.
labels.tag-projects-help: Without this, the tag is offered only in the projects below. With no project below, it is offered in all of them.
labels.show-changes: Show what the new name changes
labels.preview-truncated: More issues change than this list shows.
labels.combine-help: Every issue that has this one gets the other one instead, and this one is gone. This cannot be taken back.
labels.combine-dialog-text: The issues that have {name} get {other}, and {name} is gone.
labels.none-to-pick: This project has no labels yet.
labels.nothing-to-add: Every label is on this issue already.
many-changes.title: {action}: {count, plural, one {# issue} other {# issues}}
preview.summary: {changed, plural, =0 {No issue} one {# issue} other {# issues}} will change{skipped, plural, =0 {} one {, # will be skipped} other {, # will be skipped}}.
preview.label: Issues in this change
many-changes.project-list: Projects to move the issues to
many-changes.delete-text: The issues go to the trash. You can undo this for a short while.
many-changes.dialog-text: Check what changes first. An issue that changed since you looked is skipped, not overwritten.
many-changes.note-type-not-used: {project} does not offer {type}. The issue keeps it.
many-changes.background-note: These are many issues, so Bugaboo makes the change in the background. You can go on working.
many-changes.result-done: {changed, plural, =0 {No issue was} one {# issue was} other {# issues were}} changed{skipped, plural, =0 {} one {, # was skipped} other {, # were skipped}}.
many-changes.progress: {total, plural, one {{done} of # issue done} other {{done} of # issues done}}
many-changes.stopped: The change stopped. Some issues are changed and the rest are not.
layouts.intro: A layout says which fields a form shows, in which sections, and for which roles. A Guest can get a short form and a Team member the full one. A layout never shows a field to a role whose field permissions hide it.
layouts.not-customized: This form has not been customized yet. It shows the usual fields to every role.
layouts.inherited-organization: This form uses the layout of the whole organization.
layouts.inherited-project: This form uses the layout of {project}.
layouts.fixed: The title and the issue type are always asked for.
layouts.section-tab-help: Sections with the same tab are shown together under that tab. Leave it empty for no tabs.
layouts.section-empty: No fields in this section yet. Drag a field here or use its Add button.
layouts.available: Fields that are not on this form
layouts.available-none: Every field is on this form.
layouts.field-required: Must be filled in: it stays on the form for everybody who can fill it in.
layouts.limited-page: {role} cannot see {field}: the field permissions hide it.
layouts.limited-form: {role} cannot fill in {field}: the field permissions do not allow it.
layouts.lost: Not saved yet: someone took over, or your editing time ran out. Your changes are kept here. Choose Try again to save them.
layouts.inherited-hidden: This form uses a layout that is set higher up.
layouts.unreadable: The layout of this form could not be read, so only the basic fields are shown. Reload the page to try again.
layouts.draft-changed: This layout changed while you were editing, and you see it as it is now. Your changes from {when} are kept. Putting them back replaces what you see now.
layouts.roles-hidden: Which roles see a field is set by people who may decide what roles see.
layouts.use-inherited-text: The layout of this place is taken away. The place then goes back to the layout that counts here without a layout of its own. This cannot be undone.
layouts.delete-held: {name} is editing this layout, so it cannot be taken away yet. Try again when they have finished.
workflows.intro: A workflow says which statuses an issue can have and which status changes are allowed between them. Change it as a draft, try it, and publish it when it is right.
workflows.uses-organization: These issues use the workflow {name} of the whole organization.
workflows.uses-project: These issues use the workflow {name} of {project}.
workflows.uses-hidden: These issues use the workflow {name}, which is set higher up.
workflows.uses-starting: These issues use the starter workflow {name}.
workflows.use-inherited-text: The workflow of this place is taken away, and the place goes back to the workflow that counts here without a workflow of its own. This cannot be undone, and it is refused while it would leave an issue in a status that the workflow then counting does not have.
workflows.delete-held: {name} is editing this workflow, so it cannot be taken away yet. Try again when they have finished.
workflows.name: Name of the workflow
workflows.statuses-help: New issues start in the first status. Renaming a status does not move the issues that are in it.
workflows.status-name-taken: A status with this name exists already.
workflows.publish-name-twice: Two statuses are called {name}. Give one of them another name, then publish.
workflows.no-changes: No status change starts here yet.
workflows.change-remove: Remove the status change from {from} to {to}
workflows.rules-intro: From {from} to {to}. A rule that is left empty does not apply.
workflows.who-help: Tick nobody, and everybody who may change the issue can do it. A rule never gives a right that the person does not have.
workflows.who-assigned: The person it is assigned to
workflows.only-if-help: Everything listed here must be true before the change can happen.
workflows.must-fill-help: These fields need a value before the change can happen.
workflows.ask-for-help: These fields are asked for in a small form while the change happens. The description cannot be asked for: it is written on the issue page.
workflows.draft-note: These changes are a draft: they count only after you publish them.
workflows.lost: Not published yet: someone took over, or your editing time ran out. Your changes are kept here. Choose Try again to publish them.
workflows.draft-changed: This workflow changed while you were editing, and you see it as it is now. Your changes are kept.
workflows.publish-text: Issues are still in statuses that you removed. Choose a status for each group of issues. They move when you publish, and each move is written in the history.
workflows.publish-where: {count, plural, one {# issue is in {status}. It goes to} other {# issues are in {status}. They go to}}
workflows.publish-unseen: {count, plural, one {# of them is an issue} other {# of them are issues}} that you cannot see.
workflows.publish-blocked: {count, plural, one {# issue} other {# issues}} in {status} cannot be moved by you, so this workflow cannot be published yet.
workflows.publish-too-many: More than {limit} issues are in the statuses you removed. Move some of them first, then publish.
workflows.publish-go: Publish and move {count, plural, one {# issue} other {# issues}}
workflows.try-text: Pick an issue and a person to see which status changes they would get, and why.
workflows.try-not-for-you: This person may not change the status of this issue at all.
workflows.try-not-named: Who can do it does not name this person.
workflows.try-needs: Possible once these fields have a value: {fields}.

setting.notifications.assigned-in-app.na: An issue is assigned to you: in the app
setting.notifications.assigned-in-app.he: Tells you under Notifications when an issue is assigned to you.
setting.notifications.assigned-by-mail.n: An issue is assigned to you: by e-mail
setting.notifications.assigned-by-mail.h: Sends you an e-mail when an issue is assigned to you. E-mail goes only when your organization has switched it on.
setting.notifications.followed-activity-: Status changes, comments and files on issues you follow: in the app
Tells you under Notifications when somebody else changes the status of an issue you follow, or comments on it or adds a file to it.

setting.notifications.followed-fields-in: Other changes to issues you follow: in the app

setting.notifications.followed-fields-by: Other changes to issues you follow: by e-mail

setting.notifications.run-ended-in-app.n: Your change to many issues has ended: in the app

Your change to many issues has ended: by e-mail

setting.notifications.edit-notice-in-app: Somebody asks you to finish editing: in the app

setting.notifications.edit-notice-by-mai: Somebody asks you to finish editing: by e-mail

setting.mail.enabled.name: Send e-mail
setting.mail.enabled.help: Bugaboo sends e-mail only when this is on. Enter the mail server first and try it with Send me a test e-mail.
setting.mail.host.name: Mail server
setting.mail.host.help: The name of the mail server Bugaboo sends e-mail through, like mail.example.com. Write only that name, without a path.
setting.mail.port.name: Mail server port
setting.mail.port.help: The port of the mail server, as the provider of your mail server tells you. It depends on how the connection is protected.
setting.mail.security.name: Protect the connection
setting.mail.security.help: How the connection to the mail server is protected. Choose no encryption only for a mail server on the same computer or in a place you trust: the password and the e-mails could be read on the way.
setting.mail.username.name: Mail server user name
setting.mail.username.help: The user name Bugaboo signs in to the mail server with. Leave it empty for a mail server that asks for none. The password is entered separately and is stored encrypted.
setting.mail.from.name: Send e-mail from
setting.mail.from.help: The e-mail address that e-mails from Bugaboo come from, like bugaboo@example.com.
setting.mail.short.name: Short e-mails
setting.mail.short.help: E-mails leave out all issue text (titles and comments) and the names of projects, and only say that something happened, with a way to open it in Bugaboo. Use this where e-mail leaves the company.
error.mail.rejected: The mail server did not accept the e-mail. Check the user name and the password, and the address e-mails are sent from.
error.mail.unavailable: Bugaboo could not reach the mail server. Check the mail server, its port and the connection, then try again.
error.mail.off: E-mail is not set up. Enter the mail server and switch e-mail on first.
mail.subject: Bugaboo: {issue} {title}
mail.subject-run: Bugaboo: your change to many issues has ended
mail.subject-ids-failed: Bugaboo: new issue IDs could not be given out
mail.footer: You get this e-mail because of your notification settings. You can change them in Bugaboo under {settings} › {page}.
mail.test-text: This is a test e-mail from Bugaboo. If you can read it, Bugaboo can send e-mail.
setting.security.log-keep-days.name: Days to keep the security log
setting.security.log-keep-days.help: How many days the security log keeps its entries. Older entries are deleted once a day. A signed note of what was deleted stays, so you can still check that nobody changed the log.
setting.logs.server-log-megabytes.name: Size of the server log file
setting.logs.server-log-megabytes.help: A server that runs as a service writes its log to a file. When the file is bigger than this many megabytes, Bugaboo starts a new one and keeps the old one next to it.
setting.logs.server-log-files.name: Old server log files to keep
setting.logs.server-log-files.help: How many old files of the server log are kept next to the current one. Older ones are deleted.
mail.sign-up-exists-subject: Bugaboo: you already have an account
error.handle.changed-lately: You changed your handle only a short time ago. You can change it again later.
mail.line-more: There is more than this e-mail holds. Open it in Bugaboo to read it all.
projects.offered-in-rows: Offered where the lines say so. A project follows the project above it until it has a line of its own.
projects.offered-in-pick-first: Pick a project, or the whole organization, to add a line.
projects.offered-in-created-project: Created in {project}. Offered there and below until a line says otherwise.
issue-types.project-intro: Switch off the issue types this project does not use. Issues keep the type they have.
issue-types.project-create-title: Create an issue type for this project
issue-types.project-create-intro: A type created here is offered in this project and below.
labels.project-intro: Switch off the label groups this project does not offer. Labels already on an issue stay on it.
labels.project-create-title: Create a label group for this project
labels.project-create-intro: A label group created here is offered in this project and below.
labels.project-create-label-title: Create a label for this project
labels.project-create-label-intro: A label goes into one of the label groups of this project.
check-access.for-issue-type: The field levels are for issues of the type {type}.
error.mail.insecure: The mail server is set to send its user name or password without encryption to another computer. Switch encryption on, or use a mail server on this computer.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.nothing-all: You have no notifications yet. You hear of mentions, of issues assigned to you and of what happens on issues you follow.
notifications.news: There is news on this issue
notifications.taken-over: {who} took over the editing. What you wrote is kept as your draft
notifications.let-go: {who} ended your editing because it was stuck, so others can edit again
notifications.run-done: Your change to many issues is done
notifications.run-failed: Your change to many issues stopped before it was done
notifications.issue-ids-failed: Bugaboo could not give every issue of {project} its new ID. Open the project settings to try again
notifications.issue-ids-failed-short: Bugaboo could not give every issue of a project its new ID
notifications.issue-ids-failed-hidden: Bugaboo could not give the issues of a project their new IDs. You cannot see that project any more
notifications.customize-intro: Choose for each kind of event whether you hear of it in the app, by e-mail, in both or not at all. You never hear of your own changes. E-mail goes only when your organization has switched it on.
mail-server.title: E-mail & notifications
mail-server.intro: Bugaboo sends e-mail through your organization's mail server. E-mail stays off until you have entered the mail server, tried it with a test e-mail and switched it on.
mail-server.password-help: It is stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave the box empty to keep the password you have. If you change the mail server, the port or the user name, the password is removed: a new mail server needs its password again.
mail-server.no-encryption-note: Without encryption, a user name or a password is only accepted when the mail server is on this computer.
mail-server.test-intro: Bugaboo sends one e-mail to your address, {email}, through the mail server as you saved it.
mail-server.test-done: The test e-mail was sent to {email}. Check your e-mail.
mail-server.test-wait: You can send another test e-mail in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}.
mail-server.sign-up-note: Signing up without an invitation needs e-mail. While e-mail is off it is closed.
first-run.mail.title: Set up e-mail (you can do this later)
first-run.mail.intro: Bugaboo can tell people by e-mail when something happens on issues they follow, and can let people sign up with their e-mail address. For that it needs your organization's mail server. You can skip this and do it later under Organization settings.
handle.title: Handle
handle.intro: Your handle is the short name people type after @ to mention you, like @ana.brandt.
handle.label: Your handle
handle.invalid: A handle can have only the letters a to z, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
handle.taken: Somebody has this handle, or had it, or a group or a role has it. Choose another one.
handle.rule-characters: A handle has only the letters a to z (no accents), digits, dots, dashes and underscores, and at most {max} characters.
handle.rule-own: Nobody else may have it, and it cannot be the handle of a group or a role.
handle.rule-weekly: You can change it once in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
handle.rule-kept: A handle you give up stays reserved for you. Comments written before still name you, but a new comment that uses it names nobody.
sign-up.check-text: If {email} can sign up here, Bugaboo sent a link to it. Open the link to choose your name and your password. It works once, for {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}.
sign-up.check-nothing: Nothing there? Look in your spam folder and check the address. Press Send me a new link.
sign-up.resend-in: You can press Send me a new link in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
sign-up.resent: If {email} can sign up here, Bugaboo sent a new link to it.
sign-up-policy.mail-off: E-mail is off, so signing up without an invitation is closed. Set up e-mail first.
